items.title: Mimetic desire, social contagion, and the fight for your true self
items.description: In 1936, a shipyard worker in Hamburg kept his arms folded while hundreds of men around him raised theirs for Hitler. Luke Burgis, author of Wanting and The One in the 99, wants to know what it takes to become that person, and he traces the answer back to the family. items.title: How to become a great conversationalist
items.description: A while back, I was at a party in London where a friend introduced me to an actress who had just been in a big theater production. I was excited to talk with her. Throughout our conversation, she asked brilliant questions, and I enjoyed answering them. She was great at making people feel seen and important. But whenever I asked her something back, with real curiosity about her life, she gave a brief, polite answer and turned the spotlight back on me: “But enough about me, tell me more about you.

items.title: What total darkness reveals about who you really are
items.description:
Could removing light be a key to discovering who you really are? 
 That’s one idea behind dark retreats*, an experience that’s about as close to a complete sensory deprivation chamber as you can get. Participants spend extended periods in total darkness, stripping away the inputs and distractions of everyday life.  
 Andrew Holecek, an interdisciplinary scholar-practitioner in Tibetan Buddhism and other nondual wisdom traditions, believes in the transformative power of dark retreats.

items.title: The ancient environmental archive hidden beneath a northern bog
items.description:
I need to move on and find my field plots, but pausing here has caused my feet to sink. They are now completely buried by peat; only my shins remain visible. items.title: Current AI is not conscious
items.description:
Is today’s AI conscious? Philosopher Ned Block says no, and he’s not alone in finding the question harder than it looks.
